# 美國數據強韌，美債漲勢暫歇，AI融資門檻升高

## 通膨利多之後，市場重新衡量利率維持高檔的代價

美國經濟數據轉強，加上聯準會官員措辭偏鷹，打斷了週四的美債漲勢。經過兩天通膨利多帶動的上漲後，2年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.16%，領跌各天期。失業金申請減少、零售銷售增加，費城聯準銀行製造業指數更大幅躍升。房市仍弱，但整體數據尚不足以讓決策者認為需求已經耗盡。

這次殖利率上升主要反映實質殖利率，而非通膨補償提高。10年期實質殖利率上升3個基點至2.35%，損益兩平通膨率反而下降1個基點至2.22%。6月CPI與PPI降溫，使近期升息機率仍遠低於週初；週四市場重新計入的，是經濟保持韌性、政策因而需要更長時間維持緊縮時，持有長天期債券所面臨的成本。

AI相關資產尤其感受到這個壓力。甲骨文遭降評至BBB-，突顯新資料中心產生收入前所需的龐大資金；投資人也質疑不斷增加的資本支出能帶來多少回報，半導體股下跌逾4%。但信用市場需求並未消失：美國短券標售順利完成，主要信用債基金幾乎持平，CoreWeave仍尋求大額貸款。阻力集中在更具體的條件上，包括發債供給、現金流遞延及薄弱的債權保障，Cotality艱難的再融資與Aston Martin債權人結盟，也反映了相同的篩選壓力。

## 需求仍穩，聯準會官員不急著宣告通膨已受控

6月零售與餐飲銷售月增0.2%，5月增幅則上修至1.0%。細項並不一致：汽車經銷商與非店面零售各增1.9%，加油站銷售額下降5.3%。扣除汽車後，銷售月減0.2%；扣除汽油則增加0.7%，同時扣除兩者後增加0.4%。燃料收入下降壓低了總額，卻不代表家庭各類支出都同步退縮。

初領失業金人數降至20.8萬，續領降至180.5萬。費城聯準銀行活動指數由10.3跳升至41.4，新訂單達37.0、出貨33.7；支付價格指數小升至53.9，收取價格升至27.4。不過，企業對未來6個月較不樂觀，活動與資本支出預期均下降。5月企業銷售增加2.1%，庫存只增0.3%，使庫存銷售比降至1.28。

房市最明顯反映了高利率的抑制作用。建商信心降至34，37%的建商降價、63%提供促銷誘因。這與當前製造業的強勁形成對比：經濟不是全面強勢，而是利率敏感產業仍吃力，勞動市場卻尚未廣泛轉弱。

達拉斯聯準銀行總裁洛根認為，小幅提高利率更能平衡前景。要讓通膨回到2%，仍仰賴服務價格持續降溫、能源不再帶來新壓力，以及需求不進一步增強。堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁施密德也強調，能源以外的價格壓力依然廣泛，經濟成長仍具韌性。兩人的談話都不支持僅憑一個月的好數據，就認定政策爭論已有定論。

交換市場對7月29日仍只計入約3個基點升息，相當於約13%的升息25個基點機率，週初則約為40%。到12月的升息定價約29個基點，低於本週稍早的43個基點。交易員持續賣出9月、12月SOFR賣權，解除對利率上升的避險。因此，週四短端回跌，仍發生在整週近期升息押注大幅減少的背景下。

5年期殖利率上升2個基點至4.28%，10年期升2個基點至4.57%，30年期升1個基點至5.09%。曲線小幅趨平，2s10s收窄1個基點至41個基點，2s30s收窄2個基點至93個基點。相較一個月前，2年期仍高9個基點，30年期高12個基點。各觀察天期的實質殖利率均上升3個基點，除10年期外，5年期達2.04%、7年期2.18%、20年期2.71%、30年期2.91%。

長端方面，Hoisington的立場轉變呈現了更深層的疑慮。這家看多美債逾30年的機構轉為看空，理由包括財政赤字、資金需求，以及更高的通膨均衡水準；它預估長期通膨區間為3.5%至4.5%，部分時期可能超過5%。旗下基金先前存續期間約20.9年，遠高於綜合債券指數的約6年。這項投資判斷不同於當天數據引起的波動，卻顯示超長存續期間策略的基礎，取決於遠超過下一次聯準會會議的假設。

短期資金市場承接供給則未出現相同壓力。$1,000億8週券得標利率為3.650%，投標倍數2.84倍；競標分配中，間接投標人取得$654.70億、交易商$275.15億、直接投標人$37.97億。$1,100億4週券得標利率3.660%，投標倍數2.57倍，分別分配$549.49億予間接投標人、$417.53億予交易商、$56.44億予直接投標人。兩檔都在7月21日交割。

稍晚美東19:00發布的傑佛遜談話報導，延續了這種附帶條件的政策立場：目前政策位置合適，但若通膨未能降溫，仍可能重新考慮。他將AI描述為需求衝擊先到、而生產力效益尚不確定，能源也可能影響通膨預期。這是收盤後對政策辯論的補充，而非稍早美債走勢的新增驅動因素。

## AI融資與高槓桿再融資，開始面對更嚴格的條件

標普將甲骨文降至最低投資級BBB-，因為$2,500億的資料中心擴張，跑在收入與現金生成能力之前。過去4季扣除資本支出後，自由現金流缺口已超過$200億；標普估計新會計年度可能擴大至$420億。穆迪的負向展望也意味著仍有另一條降評風險。

甲骨文債券價格早已反映部分信用惡化。其10年期債殖利率約6.4%，同天期BBB曲線為5.7%，BB債則為6.7%。2月發行$250億後，甲骨文在一項主要美國公司債指數中的規模約達$1,170億，公司並預計於本會計年度透過債務與股權籌措約$400億。若遭兩家評等機構降至非投資級，這個超大型發行人可能移入規模較小的高收益債投資人群體，因此後續選擇借款還是增資，對債權人尤其重要。

供給疑慮並不限於甲骨文。大型雲端業者債券已占廣泛投資級指數市值約4%至5%，超出預期的發行使利差走擴。CoreWeave正尋求$26億延遲動用定期貸款，依照最低付款承諾合約安裝GPU；公司年度支出計畫超過$340億，先前$31億GPU擔保貸款則吸引$190億訂單。合約需求與資產擔保結構仍能帶來資金，但公開債券市場也開始要求補償這個產業權重不斷增加的風險。

Cotality，即原CoreLogic，面對的阻力更直接。美債收盤後不久發布的消息指出，這家房地產資料公司考慮把第一順位債殖利率由8%中段提高至最高9.5%，第二順位則由11%提高至約12%，後者還可能折價發行，並增加投資人保障。這筆$53億再融資訂單反應冷淡，背景是約8倍槓桿、現金僅約$5,500萬，自由現金流非常有限，且預期需更多動用循環額度。

公司標普評等比投資級低6級，這次處理的是5年前$60億收購所留下的債務。更高殖利率會進一步增加原已吃緊的現金負擔，文件調整則關係到營運不如預期時，各方能分得多少價值。討論中的讓步因此攸關交易能否完成，而不只是對既定價格做小幅修飾。

Aston Martin債權人則在新融資可能改變順位之前先行結盟。股東提供£5,000萬債務支援流動性後，以Arini、BlackRock及Sculptor為首的基金聘請Jefferies。該集團持有公司$18.5億等值2029年到期債券的多數，並簽訂合作協議，擔心寬鬆文件可能容許新融資排在既有債權之前。產品延後、中國需求疲弱與美國關稅，使順位保障更加迫切。

其他產業也有各自的資金與估值問題。美國銀行停止協助芝加哥出售約$10億逾期罰款及費用應收款的計畫。交易原估至少帶來$8,900萬，進展受阻成為年中預估$9,000萬收入缺口的原因之一。困難在於將無擔保應收款變現，而非同等金額的一般稅收短缺。

高收益博彩業利差今年擴大約9個基點，同期消費循環產業卻收窄約17個基點，反映實體賭場成長放緩，以及線上博彩、預測市場的競爭。航運方面，花旗建議放空達飛海運債券，認為荷莫茲局勢帶來的行情過後，新增船舶運能將威脅運價。其€7億、2032年到期債券交易價格約99.5，較3月底高約6點。

主要基金遠比這些個別消息平靜：LQD下跌0.07%至107.50，HYG下跌0.01%至79.80，JNK上漲0.01%至96.08。這些價格沒有顯示資金全面撤離信用市場。融資消息呈現的反而是更細緻的篩選：槓桿、債權順位、產業供給與現金生成時點，正在決定資金願意以什麼條件留下。

## 南韓升息、債券卻漲，日本面對偏高的通膨預期

南韓央行一致決議將7天附買回利率提高25個基點至2.75%，為2023年1月以來首次升息，並保留緊縮傾向。總裁申鉉松指出，通膨、成長增強、韓元偏弱與金融穩定風險，都使每次會議有可能調整政策。但南韓3年期、10年期殖利率反而各降4個基點至3.83%、4.29%。升息原已被充分預期，而央行沒有暗示要加快步伐，讓債券得以上漲；交換市場仍計入未來6個月至少再升息兩次。

申鉉松認為，半導體出口大增後，先前2.6%的成長預估看來過低，6月通膨則已達3.2%。AI循環一方面改善活動與貿易條件，一方面也增加價格壓力。對債券投資人而言，重要差別在於這是已預期的正常化一步，還是足以把後續整條利率路徑都往上移的新證據。

日本家庭調查則突顯另一種政策兩難。未來5年平均通膨預期升至10.8%，創2006年有紀錄以來新高，中位數仍為5%。6月政策利率升至1%後，市場估計10月以前再調整利率的機率約66%。但在7月31日決議前，同時有創紀錄的24%家庭認為利率已經太高。

日本短期工具仍有買盤。1年期短券接受¥2.136兆競標，最低得標價格對應殖利率1.2168%，加權平均殖利率1.2066%，另接受¥6,644億非競標。流動性增強操作則發行¥6,990億、剩餘年期1至5年的債券，平均利差為−0.004%。即使預期的日本銀行政策路徑提高了國內投資人可取得的報酬，這些操作仍顯示供給能被承接。

英國5月GDP月增0.1%，4月修正為下降0.1%，近3個月成長0.7%。服務業增加0.3%，生產下降0.5%，營建下降0.8%。英國央行副總裁布里登認為，經濟閒置與較高借款成本降低了能源衝擊固化的風險，但若出現第二輪效應，仍可升息。因此，利率敏感產業偏弱，與服務業成長、能源前景不明同時存在。

法國的限制更直接來自財政。財政部委託的分析估計，下一任總統需在5年內節省€1,260億，才足以穩定債務；若不採取行動，2030年財政缺口可能接近GDP的7%，主要原因是債息成本。這替既有法債財政疑慮增加了具體量化：殖利率提高，正擴大未來政府必須完成的調整。

## 衝突與債務協商壓力，主導新興市場個別風險

EMB下跌0.15%至95.59，美元指數上升0.23%至100.73。較高美國實質殖利率與較強美元形成共同逆風，但現券最明顯的惡化來自中東。區域平均主權利差一週擴大約20個基點，至美債之上402個基點，創2022年10月以來最高，並比其他新興市場發行人高163個基點。

4月停火破裂、荷莫茲周邊再遭攻擊，使中東美元債出現戰爭開始以來在新興市場中的最差表現。對產油國而言，價格上漲未必足以抵銷干擾：出口中斷可能減少財政收入，安全、航運與保險成本卻增加。週四原油小跌，也無法解決海峽通行能否持續、長期投資計畫能否落實的不確定性。

塞內加爾債務爭論則有了更明確的估值比較。花旗以重整後殖利率11%與9%估算，每$1面額回收價值為43至50美分，低於債券當時51至54美分的價格。公共債務接近GDP的130%，IMF計畫仍暫停。花旗認為核心是財政與債務可持續性，而非眼前國際收支不足。聘任Lazard、較長天期區域債需求轉弱，已讓協商更接近現實，即使官方仍反對重整；新增回收率估計則說明，單靠區域借款難以回答既有債券究竟值多少。

中國收緊的是另一條再融資管道。銀行間市場監管機關告知部分銀行人士，地方融資平台若債券餘額高於2023年3月31日水準，應暫停進行中的銷售並避免新發行。平台債餘額約CNY16兆，其中約CNY5兆在2027年底前到期，52.7%在銀行間市場交易。限制供給可能增加流通券稀缺性，卻也讓既有債務最重的發行人更難再融資。

收盤後，莫三比克表示，正與最大雙邊債權人中國就約$14.5億債務展延取得進展，並以4月與巴西的協議為參考：當時約$1.43億債務改為先支付一筆款項，再以3.625%利率、每半年一次分10期償付。潛在$300億LNG計畫尚需時間才能改善中期財政，在此之前，債務紓緩與新IMF計畫仍有迫切性；IMF依然將該國列為債務困境。

## 實質殖利率回升，放大AI回報較晚到位的壓力

S&P 500下跌0.51%至7,533.77，Nasdaq 100下跌1.62%至29,025.77，半導體指數重挫4.29%至11,867.50，VIX上升6.76%至16.73。科技股跌勢最重，與AI債務的融資疑慮呼應，而非所有風險資產同步撤退。

台積電展望強勁，卻未能阻止半導體股下跌，因為更高的資本支出指引加深了對未來回報的疑問。美國四大業者今年預計支出超過$7,250億；Alphabet另因旗艦模型進度落後的報導而走弱。甲骨文降評讓債券投資人從資產負債表看到相同問題：支出先發生、收入較晚到來，實質殖利率提高，使這段時間差更昂貴。

油價連漲三天後暫歇。WTI下跌0.82%至$78.95，布蘭特下跌0.85%至$84.23，但一週漲幅仍達9.53%、10.39%。美國本土48州天然氣庫存增加410億立方英尺至3.024兆立方英尺，主要來自中西部與東部。當日能源回落伴隨美債損益兩平通膨率下降，但先前累積的油價漲幅與最新攻擊，仍使後續燃料及運費前景不明。

美元轉強、實質殖利率提高之際，黃金期貨下跌1.44%至$3,985.60。地緣政治惡化並未在這個環境下形成全面避險上漲。債券、匯率與科技股共同反映的，是實質融資成本重新施壓，儘管美債本身的跌幅仍然溫和。

## 週五確認需求韌性與價格降溫能否並存

7月17日美東08:30公布進出口物價與新屋開工，09:15為工業生產及產能利用率，10:00為密西根大學消費者信心初值。這些數據將一起顯示，建商信心及調查預期轉弱是否擴散，或者當前產出仍強。家庭通膨預期與貿易價格也有助於判斷，物價改善是可持續趨勢，還是暫時有利的一個月。

同日05:00有歐元區6月通膨終值，接著是7月22日10:30的美國石油報告，以及7月23日08:15的ECB決議。6月物價需要搭配更新的庫存與航運狀況解讀；即使原油價格下跌，中東主權利差仍可補充反映衝突風險究竟消退多少。

供給方面，7月20日有$920億13週券與$790億26週券，7月21日有$950億6週券，均在7月23日交割。7月22日則有日本約¥3,000億40年期公債，以及美東13:00的美國$130億20年期增額標售。短券已有買盤，更長天期的標售將測試高殖利率能否吸引願意承擔存續期間風險的投資人。企業端可看Cotality最終條件，確認高槓桿借款人需要提供多少額外殖利率與債權保障，才能完成再融資。

# Firm US data check the bond rally as AI borrowers face a higher financing bar

## Inflation relief meets the cost of staying restrictive

Stronger US activity and a firmer message from Fed officials interrupted the Treasury rally on Thursday. The 2-year yield rose 3 basis points to 4.16%, leading a modest selloff after two sessions of inflation relief. Jobless claims declined, retail sales increased and the Philadelphia Fed's manufacturing gauge surged. Housing remained weak, but the combined releases gave policymakers little reason to regard demand as exhausted.

The move came through real yields rather than higher inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield rose 3 basis points to 2.35%, while its breakeven fell 1 to 2.22%. June's softer CPI and PPI still left an immediate Fed increase much less likely than at the start of the week. What Thursday restored was some of the cost of holding duration if growth stays firm and policy remains restrictive for longer.

That cost was particularly visible in AI-related assets. Oracle's downgrade to BBB- sharpened attention on the cash required before new data centers generate revenue; semiconductor shares fell more than 4% as investors questioned the returns on rising capital expenditure. Yet demand for credit had not disappeared. Short Treasury auctions cleared, broad credit funds barely moved and CoreWeave pursued another large loan. The resistance was more specific: investors wanted compensation for supply, delayed cash flow and weak creditor protections, as Cotality's difficult refinancing and Aston Martin bondholders' organizing efforts also showed.

## Demand holds up, and Fed officials resist declaring victory

June retail and food-service sales rose 0.2%, following an upwardly revised 1.0% increase in May. The composition was uneven. Auto dealers and nonstore retailers each gained 1.9%, while gasoline-station receipts fell 5.3%. Sales excluding autos declined 0.2%, but excluding gasoline they rose 0.7%; excluding both, the increase was 0.4%. Lower fuel receipts softened the headline without indicating a comparable retreat across household spending.

Initial jobless claims fell to 208,000 and continuing claims to 1.805 million. The Philadelphia Fed activity index jumped to 41.4 from 10.3, with new orders at 37.0 and shipments at 33.7. Prices paid edged up to 53.9 and prices received rose to 27.4. Businesses were less confident about the next six months, however, with activity and capital-spending expectations declining. May business sales rose 2.1% against a 0.3% inventory increase, reducing the inventory-to-sales ratio to 1.28.

Housing provided the clearest evidence of restraint. Builder confidence fell to 34; 37% of builders cut prices and 63% offered incentives. The contrast with current manufacturing activity left a mixed, rather than uniformly strong, economy—one in which rate-sensitive sectors were struggling without a broader labor-market break.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said modestly higher rates would better balance the outlook. Returning inflation to 2% depended on continued services moderation, no renewed energy pressure and demand that did not strengthen further. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid likewise emphasized broad price pressure beyond energy alongside resilient growth. Their comments challenged the idea that one favorable month of inflation settled the policy debate.

Swaps still priced only about 3 basis points of tightening for July 29, roughly a 13% probability of a quarter-point increase, versus about 40% at the week's start. December carried around 29 basis points of tightening, down from 43 earlier in the week. Traders continued selling September and December SOFR puts to close protection against higher rates. Thursday's front-end cheapening therefore sat within a larger weekly retreat from near-term hike bets.

The 5-year Treasury yield rose 2 basis points to 4.28%, the 10-year 2 to 4.57% and the 30-year 1 to 5.09%. The curve flattened modestly: 2s10s narrowed 1 basis point to 41 and 2s30s 2 to 93. Over the month, yields remained 9 basis points higher at two years and 12 higher at 30 years. Real yields rose 3 basis points at every quoted maturity, taking five years to 2.04%, seven to 2.18%, 20 to 2.71% and 30 to 2.91%, alongside the increase at ten years.

At the long end, Hoisington's change of view illustrated a more structural concern. After more than 30 years of Treasury bullishness, the firm turned bearish, citing deficits, capital demand and a higher inflation equilibrium. It estimated long-run inflation at 3.5%–4.5%, with episodes above 5%. Its fund had previously carried duration near 20.9 years, compared with roughly six for the Aggregate index. That investment judgment was distinct from the day's data-driven move, but showed how much the case for extreme duration depends on assumptions beyond the next Fed meeting.

Cash supply was absorbed without a comparable disturbance. The $100 billion, 8-week bill auction cleared at 3.650% with 2.84 times coverage; indirect bidders received $65.470 billion of competitive awards, dealers $27.515 billion and direct bidders $3.797 billion. The $110 billion, 4-week sale cleared at 3.660% with 2.57 times coverage, awarding $54.949 billion to indirects, $41.753 billion to dealers and $5.644 billion to directs. Both settle July 21.

Later in the evening, a 19:00 ET account of Vice Chair Philip Jefferson's remarks added a conditional message: policy was well positioned, but could be reconsidered if inflation failed to cool. He described AI as a demand shock arriving before uncertain productivity benefits, with energy another possible influence on expectations. The remarks extended the debate beyond the close rather than constituting another driver of the earlier Treasury move.

## AI funding and leveraged refinancings draw sharper distinctions

S&P cut Oracle to BBB-, the lowest investment-grade tier, as a $250 billion data-center expansion ran ahead of revenue and cash generation. Free cash flow after capital spending had been more than $20 billion negative over the preceding four quarters; S&P estimated that the deficit could reach $42 billion in the coming fiscal year. Moody's negative outlook left open another route toward a downgrade.

Oracle's bonds already reflected some of that deterioration. Its 10-year debt yielded about 6.4%, versus 5.7% for the 10-year BBB curve and 6.7% for BB debt. About $117 billion of Oracle bonds sat in a major US corporate index after a $25 billion February sale, and the company expected to raise roughly $40 billion through debt and equity during the fiscal year. Losing investment grade at two agencies could move an unusually large issuer into a smaller high-yield investor base, making the choice between further borrowing and equity especially consequential.

The supply concern extended beyond Oracle. Hyperscaler bonds had reached about 4%–5% of the broad investment-grade index by market value, with spreads widening as issuance exceeded expectations. CoreWeave was seeking a $2.6 billion delayed-draw term loan to install GPUs under take-or-pay contracts. Its annual spending plans exceeded $34 billion, following a $3.1 billion GPU-backed loan that attracted $19 billion of orders. Contracted demand and asset-backed structures continued to mobilize financing even as public bond investors demanded more compensation for the sector's growing weight.

Cotality, formerly CoreLogic, faced more immediate resistance. In an update published shortly after the Treasury close, the property-data company was considering a yield as high as 9.5% on first-lien bonds, up from the mid-8% area, and about 12% on a second-lien tranche, up from 11%. The latter could be issued below par, alongside stronger investor protections. Its $5.3 billion refinancing had drawn lukewarm orders against roughly eight-times leverage, only about $55 million of cash and expectations of greater revolver use while free cash flow remained very modest.

The company, rated six notches below investment grade by S&P, was refinancing debt from a $6 billion acquisition five years earlier. Higher yields would add debt service to an already thin liquidity position; documentation changes would determine how value was shared if operations disappointed. The concessions under discussion were therefore central to whether the transaction could clear, not just an adjustment to an otherwise settled price.

Aston Martin creditors were organizing before additional financing could alter their position. Funds led by Arini, BlackRock and Sculptor hired Jefferies after shareholders provided £50 million of debt for liquidity. The group held a majority of the automaker's $1.85 billion equivalent of 2029 bonds and entered a cooperation agreement amid concern that loose documentation could allow new financing to subordinate existing claims. Product delays, weak Chinese demand and US tariffs made that priority question more pressing.

Other sectors had their own financing or valuation problems. Bank of America stopped working with Chicago on a plan to sell about $1 billion of overdue fines and fees. The proposed transaction was expected to raise at least $89 million; its lack of progress contributed to a projected $90 million midyear revenue gap. The difficulty lay in monetizing unsecured receivables, rather than an equivalent shortfall in ordinary tax collections.

High-yield gaming spreads had widened about 9 basis points during the year while consumer-cyclical spreads narrowed about 17, as land-based casinos faced slower growth and competition from online betting and prediction markets. In shipping, Citi recommended shorting CMA CGM debt, arguing that new vessel capacity threatened freight rates after the Hormuz-related rally. Its €700 million, 2032 bond traded near 99.5, about six points above end-March.

Broad funds were much quieter than these individual stories: LQD fell 0.07% to 107.50, HYG 0.01% to 79.80 and JNK rose 0.01% to 96.08. There was no generalized withdrawal from credit in those prices. The day's financing news instead showed how leverage, creditor ranking, industry supply and the timing of cash generation were determining the terms on which money remained available.

## Korea hikes into a bond rally; Japan confronts high inflation expectations

The Bank of Korea unanimously raised its 7-day repurchase rate 25 basis points to 2.75%, its first increase since January 2023, and retained a tightening bias. Governor Shin Hyun Song cited inflation, stronger growth, a weak won and financial-stability risks, keeping every meeting live. Yet Korean 3- and 10-year yields fell 4 basis points to 3.83% and 4.29%. The increase had been fully anticipated, and the absence of guidance toward faster tightening allowed bonds to rally even as swaps retained at least two further increases over six months.

Shin said the earlier 2.6% growth projection looked too low after a semiconductor-led export boom; June inflation had reached 3.2%. The AI cycle was supporting activity and the terms of trade while also contributing to price pressure. For bondholders, the distinction was between an expected normalization step and evidence that the entire subsequent path needed to move higher.

Japan's household survey underscored its own policy tension. Average inflation expectations over the next five years reached 10.8%, the highest since records began in 2006, although the median remained 5%. About 66% probability was attached to another BOJ move by October after the policy rate reached 1% in June. At the same time, a record 24% of households considered rates already too high ahead of the July 31 decision.

Japanese cash instruments still found buyers. A 1-year bill sale accepted ¥2.136 trillion of competitive bids, with a yield of 1.2168% at the lowest accepted price and a 1.2066% weighted-average yield, plus ¥664.4 billion of noncompetitive bids. A liquidity-enhancement operation placed ¥699.0 billion of bonds with one to five years remaining at a −0.004% average spread. These operations provided evidence of absorption, even as the expected BOJ path raised the return available to domestic investors.

Britain's May GDP rose 0.1% after a revised 0.1% April decline, leaving three-month growth at 0.7%. Services expanded 0.3%, but production fell 0.5% and construction 0.8%. BOE Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden argued that slack and higher borrowing costs reduced the risk of the energy shock becoming embedded, while leaving room to tighten if second-round effects developed. Weak rate-sensitive sectors thus coexisted with services growth and continued energy uncertainty.

France's constraint was more explicitly fiscal. A Finance Ministry-commissioned analysis estimated that the next president would need €126 billion of savings over five years merely to stabilize debt. Without action, the fiscal gap could approach 7% of output in 2030, largely because of debt-service costs. The estimate added detail to the fiscal concerns already weighing on French bonds: higher yields were increasing the adjustment future governments would need to make.

## Conflict and debt treatment weigh on emerging-market borrowers

EMB fell 0.15% to 95.59 as the dollar index rose 0.23% to 100.73. Higher US real yields and a firmer dollar were a common headwind, but the clearest cash-bond deterioration came from the Middle East. The region's average sovereign premium widened about 20 basis points over a week to 402 over Treasuries, the widest since October 2022 and 163 basis points above other emerging-market issuers.

The breakdown of the April ceasefire and renewed attacks around Hormuz had produced the region's worst performance in EM dollar bonds since the war began. For oil producers, higher prices did not necessarily offset disruption: interrupted exports could reduce fiscal receipts, while security, shipping and insurance costs rose. Thursday's small crude decline did little to resolve the uncertainty over continuing access to the strait or the viability of longer-dated investment plans.

Senegal's debt debate acquired a more explicit valuation test. Citi estimated recoveries of 43–50 cents on the dollar under exit yields of 11% and 9%, below bonds trading at 51–54 cents. Debt was near 130% of GDP and the IMF program remained suspended. The bank saw fiscal and debt sustainability, rather than an immediate balance-of-payments shortage, as the central problem. Hiring Lazard and weaker demand for longer regional securities had already brought negotiations closer despite official opposition to restructuring; the new recovery estimates showed why regional borrowing alone was unlikely to settle the question of what existing bonds were worth.

China tightened a different refinancing channel. The interbank regulator told some bankers that LGFVs with bond balances above their March 31, 2023 levels should suspend ongoing sales and avoid new offerings. The sector had about CNY16 trillion of bonds outstanding, including roughly CNY5 trillion maturing by end-2027; 52.7% traded in the interbank market. Limiting supply could create scarcity for outstanding bonds while making refinancing harder for the issuers most constrained by existing debt.

After the close, Mozambique reported progress on rescheduling roughly $1.45 billion owed to China, its largest bilateral creditor. It cited an April agreement with Brazil as a model: about $143 million was restructured into an initial payment followed by ten semiannual installments at 3.625%. Debt relief and a new IMF program were needed well before a prospective $30 billion LNG project could improve medium-term finances; the IMF still described the country as in debt distress.

## Higher real yields expose the timing of AI returns

The S&P 500 fell 0.51% to 7,533.77, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.62% to 29,025.77 and the semiconductor index dropped 4.29% to 11,867.50. VIX rose 6.76% to 16.73. Technology bore the largest losses, paralleling the financing concerns evident in AI-related debt rather than a uniform retreat across every risk asset.

Semiconductors weakened despite TSMC's strong outlook as higher capital-spending guidance intensified questions about future returns. The four largest US operators were expected to spend more than $725 billion during the year; Alphabet also fell amid reports that a flagship model was behind schedule. Oracle's downgrade gave bondholders a balance-sheet version of the same concern: the spending arrives before the revenue, and higher real yields make that interval more expensive.

Oil paused after three advances. WTI fell 0.82% to $78.95 and Brent 0.85% to $84.23, though weekly gains remained 9.53% and 10.39%. Lower-48 natural-gas inventories rose 41 Bcf to 3,024 Bcf, led by the Midwest and East. The daily energy retreat accompanied lower Treasury breakevens, while the accumulated oil gain and renewed attacks kept later fuel and freight costs uncertain.

Gold futures fell 1.44% to $3,985.60 as the dollar strengthened and real yields rose. Worsening geopolitical risk did not produce a broad haven rally in that setting. Across bonds, currencies and technology shares, the more consistent feature of the session was the renewed weight of real financing costs, even though the scale of the Treasury move remained modest.

## Friday tests whether resilient demand can coexist with softer prices

July 17 brings import and export prices and housing starts at 08:30 ET, industrial production and capacity utilization at 09:15, and preliminary University of Michigan sentiment at 10:00. Together they will show whether the weakness in builder confidence and survey expectations is spreading, or whether current output remains firm. Household inflation expectations and trade prices will also help distinguish sustainable disinflation from a temporary favorable month.

Final June euro-area inflation is due at 05:00 ET that day, followed by the next US petroleum report at 10:30 on July 22 and the ECB decision at 08:15 on July 23. June's price readings will need to be considered alongside newer inventory and shipping developments. Middle Eastern sovereign spreads provide an additional measure of how much conflict risk persists even when crude prices dip.

Supply includes $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills on July 20, then $95 billion of 6-week bills on July 21, ahead of July 23 settlements. July 22 pairs Japan's roughly ¥300 billion, 40-year sale with a $13 billion US 20-year reopening at 13:00 ET. Short bills have found demand; the longer sales will test whether elevated yields also attract investors willing to hold duration. Cotality's eventual terms offer the corporate counterpart, showing how much additional yield and creditor protection a highly leveraged borrower needs to complete its refinancing.
